_readme: Client-side rate and concurrency limits per provider (W4-04). Held in config rather than in code so a limit can be corrected from a provider console without a release — a rate limit discovered at 3am should be a config change, not a deploy. Every entry states where its numbers came from: `published` means transcribed from that provider's documented ceiling with a source link, `conservative-default` means the ceiling is not yet known and the client is deliberately slower than it needs to be. A guessed high limit and a known high limit look identical in config and behave identically right up until the provider starts refusing requests, so they are never allowed to look the same here.

defaults._readme: Applied to any provider whose published ceiling is unknown. Chosen to be comfortably below the slowest plausible published limit: being slower than necessary costs latency, while being faster than permitted costs 429s that the fallback chain will read as provider ill-health and use to open a circuit breaker. The asymmetry is what makes the conservative side the correct default.

anthropic.note: Anthropic publishes tier-dependent limits; the account's tier is not recorded here. Transcribe the real ceiling from the console at W3-07 and set basis to published.

openai.note: Tier-dependent. No alias routes here today; the entry exists so a revert to an OpenAI incumbent inherits a bounded client rather than an unbounded one.

deepseek.note: Serves llm.extract, a batch-class alias, so a longer acquire timeout is appropriate: a batch caller can afford to queue where a hot-path caller cannot.

deepinfra.note: Awaiting W3-02. Transcribe the published ceiling then.

fireworks.note: The backlog calls out recording Fireworks' published RPM ceiling specifically (W3-03 -> W4-04). Do that at onboarding.

groq.note: Declared primary of the hot-path llm.fast alias but blocked on open item OI-01. Held tighter than the default because a hot-path caller cannot afford to queue: if the limit binds, failing fast into the chain beats waiting.

openrouter.note: Aggregator backstop, reached by explicit route only. Held tight because its own limits are a function of whichever upstream it selects, which the client cannot observe.
